main_body: Large wooden crate (with a smaller crate beside it): plank-striped lid on top, dark brown front face with a diagonal brace
top_band: light tan plank-striped band, rows 1-9, with slightly darker plank lines, ending at a dark edge at row 10
evidence: Down the middle column: light tan lid rows 1-9, a dark edge/shadow row at 10, then the brown front face rows 10-18 with a diagonal brace, then a dark base shadow at rows 19-20. The lid is a clearly visible horizontal surface about 8 rows tall, and the front face sits below it. The smaller crate repeats the same structure. The brace is painted flat rather than inset, but the top and front are both clearly drawn.

style.evidence: The lid has about 3 tan tones in plain horizontal stripes. The front face is a large area of near-flat dark brown with a single-tone diagonal brace and no grain, nail or knot dots. Outlines are dark brown, which is fine. Most tiles hold only 3-4 colours, against roughly 10 per tile in the Beodeul stall and well references, so the crate reads thinner and flatter than they do.
